## Project Overview

This repository contains `class-validator`, a library for object validation based on decorators [package.json][README.md:1-11]. It allows for both decorator-based and non-decorator-based validation and is designed to work in both browser and Node.js environments [README.md:8-11]. The library is written in TypeScript and published as an NPM package [package.json][.github/workflows/continuous-deployment-workflow.yml:1-29].

The core functionality involves applying decorator functions to class properties to define validation rules. Examples of decorators include `@IsEmail`, `@IsInt`, `@MinLength`, and `@ValidateNested` for validating nested objects [README.md:53-121][sample/sample1-simple-validation/Post.ts:20-49]. The library provides functions like `validate`, `validateOrReject`, and `validateSync` to execute the validation logic and retrieve a list of errors [README.md:53-121][src/index.ts:46-60][src/index.ts:79-96].

The main technologies used are TypeScript for the source code, Jest for testing, and Rollup for creating UMD builds [package.json][jest.config.js][.eslintrc.yml]. The project internally uses the `validator.js` library for many of its validation checks [README.md:9-10][package.json].

The main entry point for the library appears to be `src/index.ts`, which exports the public API, including the core `validate` functions and various decorators [src/index.ts:46-60].

## Setup / Installation

The primary prerequisite for using this library is Node.js, with CI pipelines running on `lts/*` and `current` versions [.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:18-20]. The project uses `npm` as its package manager, and the documentation recommends using `npm@6` or higher [README.md:49-52][.github/dependabot.yml:1-15].

To install the library for use in a project, run `npm install class-validator --save` [README.md:45-52][docs/introduction/installation.md:1-8]. To install the development dependencies for contributing to this repository, the CI workflows use `npm ci --ignore-scripts` [.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:12-12].

Since the project uses decorators, you must enable `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` in your `tsconfig.json` file. This project's own `tsconfig.json` has these settings enabled [tsconfig.json].

The evidence does not specify any environment variables required for local setup or installation. The `.gitignore` file does list `.env`, which suggests they might be used, but their contents are not documented in the provided files [.gitignore].

## Running Locally

This is a library and does not have a typical `start` script for running a local server. The available scripts focus on building, testing, and code style checks [package.json]. No ports are specified in the evidence.

The local development workflow likely involves writing code and using the following scripts:
*   `npm run test`: Runs tests with coverage using Jest [package.json].
*   `npm run test:watch`: Runs Jest in watch mode [package.json].
*   `npm run prettier:check` and `npm run lint:check`: To check for code formatting and linting issues [package.json]. These are used in the CI pipeline [.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:13-14].
*   `npm run prettier:fix` and `npm run lint:fix`: To automatically fix formatting and linting issues [package.json].

The project has a multi-step build process to generate different module formats. The CI workflows run these individual build scripts:
*   `npm run build:es2015`: Compiles to ES2015 modules [package.json][tsconfig.prod.esm2015.json]
*   `npm run build:esm5`: Compiles to ES2015 modules with an ES5 target [package.json][tsconfig.prod.esm5.json]
*   `npm run build:cjs`: Compiles to CommonJS modules [package.json][tsconfig.prod.cjs.json]
*   `npm run build:umd`: Creates a UMD bundle using Rollup [package.json]
*   `npm run build:types`: Generates TypeScript declaration files [package.json][tsconfig.prod.types.json]

The main `build` script alias is `npm run build:cjs` [package.json].

## Project Structure

The codebase is organized as a TypeScript library, with source code located in the `src/` directory [tsconfig.json].

Important folders include:
*   `src/`: Contains all the source code for the library. It is further divided into:
    *   `decorator/`: Contains the implementation of all validation decorators, organized into subdirectories by category (e.g., `string`, `number`, `common`, `array`) [File list].
    *   `validation/`: Holds the core validation logic, including `Validator.ts` and the `ValidationExecutor.ts` which orchestrates the validation process [src/validation/Validator.ts:9-113][src/validation/ValidationExecutor.ts:15-437].
    *   `metadata/`: Contains classes for handling validation metadata, such as `MetadataStorage.ts` which stores all decorator information [src/metadata/MetadataStorage.ts:10-157].
    *   `validation-schema/`: Includes logic for transforming validation schemas into metadata [src/validation-schema/ValidationSchemaToMetadataTransformer.ts:9-34].
    *   `utils/`: Contains helper functions used throughout the library [src/utils/get-global.util.ts:7-31].
*   `docs/`: Project documentation, structured for GitBook [.gitbook.yaml:1-4][docs/README.md:1-38].
*   `sample/`: A directory with various usage examples [README.md:970-974].
*   `test/`: Contains functional tests for the library [File list].
*   `.github/`: Holds configuration for GitHub Actions workflows and other repository automation [.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:1-52].
*   `build/`: The output directory for all compiled files, which is excluded from version control [.gitignore][tsconfig.prod.cjs.json][tsconfig.prod.types.json].

Major files at the root of the project include:
*   `package.json`: Project manifest with scripts and dependencies.
*   `README.md`: The main documentation file with usage instructions.
*   `CHANGELOG.md`: A detailed log of changes for each version.
*   `src/index.ts`: The main entry point that exports the library's public API [src/index.ts:46-60].
*   `jest.config.js`: Configuration for the Jest test runner [jest.config.js].
*   `tsconfig.json` and other `tsconfig.*.json` files: TypeScript compiler configurations for different build targets [tsconfig.json][tsconfig.prod.cjs.json][tsconfig.spec.json].

## Testing

The project uses Jest as its testing framework, along with `ts-jest` for TypeScript support [jest.config.js][package-lock.json:11-38]. ESLint is also configured with a Jest plugin [.eslintrc.yml].

Test commands are defined in `package.json`:
*   `npm run test`: Executes `jest --coverage --verbose` [package.json].
*   `npm run test:watch`: Runs `jest --watch` for interactive development [package.json].
*   `npm run test:ci`: Runs `jest --runInBand --no-cache --coverage --verbose`, which is used in the CI pipeline [.github/workflows/continuous-integration-workflow.yml:27-27][package.json].

Test files are located in the `test/` directory, with filenames ending in `.spec.ts` (e.g., `test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts`). The `jest.config.js` is configured to collect coverage from `src/**/*.ts` files, ignoring index and interface files [jest.config.js].

The Jest configuration uses `tsconfig.spec.json` to configure the TypeScript compiler for tests [jest.config.js]. This file extends the base `tsconfig.json` and relaxes some strictness rules for the test environment [tsconfig.spec.json].

Testing patterns visible in the repository include:
*   Functional tests in the `test/functional/` directory that validate end-to-end behavior. These tests instantiate classes with decorators and use the `validator.validate()` function to check for the expected `ValidationError` objects [test/functional/nested-validation.spec.ts:7-335].
*   Unit tests for individual validator functions, located alongside the source code in files like `src/decorator/common/IsIn.spec.ts`. These tests call the validator functions directly with various inputs to check their return values [src/decorator/common/IsIn.spec.ts:3-17].
*   Tests cover various scenarios, including nested object validation (`Set`, `Map`, multi-dimensional arrays), conditional validation, promise-based validation, and error message formatting [test/functional/nested-validation.spec.ts:7-335][test/functional/conditional-validation.spec.ts:6-95][test/functional/promise-validation.spec.ts:7-155][test/functional/validation-error.spec.ts:13-90].
